_comment: Mutation testing — an AUDIT, not a CI gate.
Coverage says a line ran. It does not say the test would have noticed if the
line were wrong. Stryker changes the code (flips a <= to a <, drops a call,
returns an empty string) and reports which changes NO test caught. Those are
Scoped to src/lib on purpose: that is the pure logic — the merge engine, the
importers, the view filter, the escaping — where a wrong branch is a silent
data defect rather than a visible UI bug, and where a test can be written
cheaply. Mutating components mostly proves that a rendered string changed,
which is what the RTL suite already asserts.
Run with `npm run test:mutation`. It takes a long time (each surviving mutant
means re-running the affected tests), which is exactly why it is not in CI —
it is something you do before a release, read, and act on.

ignorePatterns carries two entries that are load-bearing rather than tidiness. '.claude' — Stryker copies the project into a sandbox, and .claude/worktrees/* holds full git checkouts that OTHER live sessions are editing; a file that vanishes between the scan and the copy fails the whole run with 'ENOENT ... copyfile'. Those worktrees are excluded through .git/info/exclude, which Stryker does not read. 'data' is the same hazard, a live SQLite DB with WAL files being written underneath the copy.

dryRunTimeoutMinutes is raised from Stryker's 5-minute default on purpose: the dry run executes the WHOLE 2600-test suite once per test-runner process, instrumented, and four of those in parallel do not finish in five minutes. The symptom is 'Initial test run timed out!' before a single mutant is tried, which reads like a broken config rather than a budget.
